purpose: decide what to test, at which level and to what depth, based on risk, so that release confidence is justified
entry_criteria: Risk areas are identified with the product owner
Environments and test data availability are known
procedure: List features and quality attributes in scope; rank by business impact and likelihood of failure.
Choose test levels per risk (unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, performance, security, accessibility) and say what each will not cover.
Define entry and exit criteria, including pass thresholds and defect severity rules.
Define environments, data, tools and who owns each activity.
Map each high risk to at least one planned test; list residual risk accepted.
Get the strategy reviewed by engineering and the product owner and baseline it.
acceptance_criteria: Every high risk maps to a planned test
Out-of-scope areas are listed with reasons
validation_method: Review by engineering lead and product owner.

validation.check: trace each high risk in the risk list to a test in the matrix
validation.expect: no high risk without a test or an accepted gap

validation.check: confirm every exit criterion has a number or a yes/no check
validation.expect: none are phrased as 'adequate' or 'good enough'

failure_modes.mode: Strategy lists tools but not risks
Only the happy path is planned
failure_modes.detection: No negative or failure scenarios in matrix
failure_modes.response: Add failure-mode tests for high-risk areas

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A payments feature ranks refund calculation as highest risk. The strategy puts heavy unit and contract testing there, a small set of end-to-end journeys, a load test for peak hour, and records that localization beyond two currencies is out of scope.
